_readme: HOW TO EDIT: each question needs an id, a prompt, and 3-4 options.
Each option has a label, a weights object (any subset of R I A S E C, values 1-3),
and optional subjects tags (secondary layer - must match tags used in courses.json).
Add or remove questions freely; the app reads whatever is in this list.
1. Keep the framing behavioural ('which would you actually do'), not self-rating.
2. Give most options a SECOND trait at weight 1. Real interests co-occur, and options
that load on a single trait produce spiky profiles that match nothing well.
Common pairings: R+I, R+C, A+I, A+E, S+E, E+C, I+C.
You do NOT need to balance how many questions offer each trait - the app normalises
each trait by its maximum attainable score before matching.

questions.prompt: It's a free Saturday and nobody needs anything from you. What actually sounds good?

options.label: Fixing up something around the house, or taking apart the thing that broke
Falling down a rabbit hole about how something works
Drawing, editing a video, or writing something for no reason
Being there for a friend who's having a rough week

questions.prompt: A group project just got assigned. Without discussing it, you drift toward...

options.label: Building the actual thing
The research and the numbers
How it looks and how it's presented
The timeline, and making sure everyone actually delivers

questions.prompt: A documentary is starting. Which one do you not switch away from?

options.label: Inside an emergency room during one full shift
How a computer chip is actually manufactured
A year in the life of an artist finishing one work
How a tiny company grew into a serious business

questions.prompt: You have to take a summer job. Which one would you mind the least?

options.label: Hardware store - stock, tools, helping people find the right part
Lab assistant - running samples, logging results
Hotel front desk - guests, all day, every day
Office records - quiet, predictable, everything filed correctly

questions.prompt: Four friends ask for help on the same day. Which one do you say yes to first?

options.label: "My laptop won't turn on."
"Can you explain this lesson? I'm completely lost."
"Can you make a poster for my event?"
"Can you help me pitch this to a sponsor?"

questions.prompt: Which of these bothers you more than it probably should?

options.label: A tool or machine left broken when it's clearly fixable
A confident argument built on bad data
Something ugly that didn't need to be ugly
A system where nobody knows who's responsible for what

questions.prompt: You have to speak in front of 200 people next month. Honest reaction?

options.label: Absolutely not. Give me something to build instead.
Fine, if I'm presenting something I actually researched
Fine, if I can make it interesting to watch
Genuinely looking forward to it

questions.prompt: Attendance isn't checked. Which class do you still show up to?

options.label: The lab or workshop with the actual equipment
Advanced math or statistics
Creative writing or studio art
Debate, psychology, or anything about why people do what they do

questions.prompt: Someone hands you 10,000 pesos and one free month. What happens to it?

options.label: Tools and parts. I'm building something.
Books and courses. I'm going deep on one topic.
Funding a short film, a zine, or a set of songs
Buying inventory and trying to turn it into 30,000
"You can fix anything."
"You always figure out why."
"Nobody else would have thought of that."
"People trust you with things that matter."

questions.prompt: Pick where you'd rather spend most of your working hours.

options.label: A workshop, a site, or outdoors
A lab, or a quiet desk with one hard problem on it
A studio with your materials everywhere
An organized office where everything has a place

questions.prompt: Five people, no assigned leader, one deadline. What do you end up doing?

options.label: Quietly doing the hands-on work
Checking whether what we're claiming is actually true
Keeping the mood up and making sure nobody gets left out
Making the calls and pushing the pace

questions.prompt: Three hours, one task, no interruptions. Which do you pick?

options.label: Assembling, wiring, or repairing something
Cleaning up a messy dataset until it makes sense
Editing a video until it finally feels right
Reconciling records until the numbers balance

questions.prompt: Which problem would you rather be handed?

options.label: "This machine keeps failing and we don't know why."
"This community has a health problem nobody's addressed."
"This brand is invisible and we need people to care."
"These records are a mess and an audit is coming."

questions.prompt: Ten years from now, which version of you feels most like the right one?

options.label: On site, hands dirty, pointing at something real that got built
The person who knows this subject cold and is asked when it's hard
Making things that make people feel something
In a room where the people you taught or led are doing well
